entrypoints.summary: Server public-key-authentication request parsing reads a protocol-provided algorithm text field before generating a key from the request.

affected_components.role: The patched identifier-to-hash policy map deletes SHA-1 mappings for ssh-rsa-family identifiers while retaining RSA-SHA2 mappings.
The server authentication parser obtains the request algorithm field.

causal_paths.kind: protocol algorithm selection to RSA hash dispatch

code_slices.fixed: Commit a448945 deletes those two SHA-1 entries and retains rsa-sha2-256 and rsa-sha2-512 hash mappings.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The same patch reads the public-key-authentication algorithm field in auth_handler and adds client preference handling for RSA-SHA2 key types.
code_slices.vulnerable: Pre-remediation RSAKey.HASHES included ssh-rsa and ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com entries selecting hashes.SHA1.

impact.affected_asset: Cryptographic algorithm-strength policy for Paramiko RSA signature authentication and verification.
impact.attacker_capability: A peer reaching the relevant SSH public-key-authentication handling can present a legacy SSH RSA algorithm identifier; further practical attacker capability is not established.
impact.security_effect: Acceptance of deprecated SHA-1 hashing for RSA signing or verification.

causal_trace.summary: An SSH public-key-authentication request supplies an algorithm text value to the server-side request parser.
RSAKey's pre-remediation identifier-to-hash dispatch included ssh-rsa and ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com entries that selected SHA-1, leaving legacy SHA-1 RSA signature identifiers supported.
RSA signature handling resolves legacy RSA algorithm identifiers through RSAKey.HASHES to the SHA-1 hash implementation instead of restricting handling to retained RSA-SHA2 identifiers.

The audited condition is HIGH-21, “Insecure parameters for digital signatures with RSA,” in Paramiko's rsakey.py component; the materials establish deprecated-hash acceptance but not a concrete forgery, downgrade, or other operational exploit outcome.

failure.operation: Identifier-to-hash dispatch for RSA signature processing selects SHA-1 for ssh-rsa-family identifiers.

primary_invariant.statement: RSA signing and verification must not accept legacy SSH RSA algorithm identifiers that select SHA-1; supported RSA signature algorithm identifiers must select modern SHA-2 hashes.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-remediation RSAKey.HASHES mapping associated ssh-rsa and ssh-rsa-cert-v01@openssh.com with hashes.SHA1.

quality.review_notes: The audit summary confirms HIGH-21 and rsakey.py scope; the inspected patch shows removal of the SHA-1 identifier mappings and the release notes confirm support removal. The bundle has no packet trace, runtime result, focused test assertion, full finding narrative, exact affected releases, or evidence of a forgery/downgrade outcome. Remote peer positioning is inferred narrowly from the patched server-side SSH public-key-authentication parser and needs review.

remediation.invariant_restored: RSA SHA-1 signing and verification support is removed, so ssh-rsa as a signature algorithm identifier is no longer accepted and RSA key handling no longer uses hashes.SHA1 for that path.
mitigation_classes: restrict RSA signature hash selection to SHA-2

affected_versions_or_commits.value: pre-remediation state before upstream commit a448945; exact released affected versions are not established by the inspected material
